Q: Update query used the wrong table in the from statement A:

The problem is basically that update [Pallet Contents] refers to a new reference to the [Pallet Contents] table. It can't see the reference within productPickLocation because that's in a different scope.

So first you have:

with productPickLocation as (
    select [Pallet Contents].*
    from [Pallet Contents]
    left join pallets on [Pallet Contents].[Pallet ID] = pallets.[Pallet ID]
    where P2CPullLocation = 1 and pallets.WarehouseID = 3
)

which actually makes an inner-join, not a left-join, due to the where clause

You then do in the main part

from #TempDiff 
inner join products on #TempDiff.SKU = products.ItemNumber
left join productPickLocation on products.[PRODUCT KEY] = productPickLocation.[Product key]

which has a left-join again, causing all products to be selected and ignoring the productPickLocation as it's logically not used.

Then you have

update [Pallet Contents]

which looks for a reference within its scope, can't find one so it cross-joins the whole table again. There is no other join condition on this implicit cross-join, so all rows got updated.

Even more interesting: the cross-join looks like an attempt to update each row multiple times. This does not happen. SQL Server detects the update is non-deterministic, and just picks one value to update. The row is only ever updated once in a single statement.

And because the set refers to a nullable column

set [Pallet Contents].Qty = [Pallet Contents].Qty - diff

the result of null - value is null, so it remained that and only the other rows were affected.

What your query should have looked like:

with productPickLocation as (
    select pc.*
    from [Pallet Contents] pc
    inner join pallets pt on pc.[Pallet ID] = pt.[Pallet ID]
    where pc.P2CPullLocation = 1
      and pt.WarehouseID = 3
)
update ppl   -- NOTE THIS LINE
set Qty -= t.diff
from productPickLocation ppl
inner join products p on p.[PRODUCT KEY] = ppl.[Product key]
inner join #TempDiff t on t.SKU = p.ItemNumber;

Or more simply:

update pc   -- NOTE THIS LINE
set Qty -= t.diff
from [Pallet Contents] pc
inner join products p on p.[PRODUCT KEY] = pc.[Product key]
inner join pallets pt on pc.[Pallet ID] = pt.[Pallet ID]
inner join #TempDiff t on t.SKU = p.ItemNumber
where pc.P2CPullLocation = 1
  and pt.WarehouseID = 3;

If the temp table isn't actually unique then you need to aggregate it first

with AggDiff as (
    select
        t.SKU,
        TotalDiff = SUM(t.diff)
    from #TempDiff t
    group by
        t.SKU
)
update pc   -- NOTE THIS LINE
set Qty -= t.TotalDiff
from [Pallet Contents] pc
inner join products p on p.[PRODUCT KEY] = pc.[Product key]
inner join pallets pt on pc.[Pallet ID] = pt.[Pallet ID]
inner join AggDiff t on t.SKU = products.ItemNumber
where pc.P2CPullLocation = 1
  and pt.WarehouseID = 3;

TL;DR;

When writing a joined update,

  • Always alias every table with a unique alias, and the update on the first line refers to the alias rather than the table name.
  • Do not use left-joins unless you've sure the logic works.
  • For clarity's sake, put the table you want to update into the from line, then ensure every join returns a single unique row (either by a join condition or by sub-aggregation).

Q: Excel VBA - [RangeName] vs Range("RangeName") A:

For list objects, I didn't know about the square bracket notation(!!!) and the other way requires knowing which sheet the listobject is in. So instead I ended up doing the following in a module:

Public Function GetListObjectsInWorkbook(wb As Workbook) As Collection
    'Note: Silly-simple, but this function existed before AddListObjectsToCollection existed
    Set GetListObjectsInWorkbook = New Collection
    AddListObjectsToCollection GetListObjectsInWorkbook, wb
End Function

Public Sub AddListObjectsToCollection(c As Collection, o)
    Dim e
    Dim oTypeName As String
    
    oTypeName = TypeName(o)
    If oTypeName = "ListObject" Then
        c.Add o, o.Name
    ElseIf (IsArray(o) Or oTypeName = "Collection" Or oTypeName = "ListObjects" Or oTypeName = "Sheets") Then
        For Each e In o
            AddListObjectsToCollection c, e
        Next e
    ElseIf oTypeName = "Workbook" Then
        AddListObjectsToCollection c, o.Sheets
    ElseIf oTypeName = "Worksheet" Then
        AddListObjectsToCollection c, o.ListObjects
    ElseIf (oTypeName = "Null" Or oTypeName = "Nothing" Or (Not IsObject(o) And IsEmpty(o))) Then
        'don't add
    Else
        Err.Raise vbObject, "Unexpected type", "AddListObjectsToCollection given unexpected " & oTypeName & " parameter"
    End If
End Sub

Public Function GetListObjectFromCollection(c As Collection, Name As String) As ListObject
    'If a ListObject is indexed as `Name` within `c`, returns it.
    'Otherwise, returns `Nothing`
    
    On Error Resume Next
    Set GetListObjectFromCollection = c.Item(Name)
End Function

So when I want access to several/all listobjects in a workbook, rather than rely on which sheet they're in or re-write code to hunt for each particular table, I can do Set colListObjects = GetListObjectsInWorkbook(wb) to get a collection of them all and then, later, I can iterate through that or use GetListObjectFromCollection(colListObjects, "TableName") to get each table I need.
